question: Born in the 1970s, this three-time World Half-Marathon champion, who won their first race at 21, was honored by the UN as Person of the Year in their country. **Tegla Chepkite Loroupe** (born 9 May 1973) is a former Kenyan [long-distance track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_track_event "Long-distance track event") and [road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") runner. She is also a global spokeswoman for peace, [women's rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_rights "Women's rights") and education. Loroupe holds the [world records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_record "World record") for 25 and 30 kilometers and previously held the world [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") record. She was the first African woman to hold the marathon World Record, which she held from 19 April 1998 until 30 September 2001. She is the three-time [World Half-Marathon champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "IAAF World Half Marathon Championships"). Loroupe was also the first woman from Africa to win the [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon"), which she has won twice. She has won marathons in London, [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam"), Hong Kong, [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin") and Rome.
In 2016, she was the person organizing the Refugee Team for the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics") in Rio.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3)

Tegla Loroupe was born in Kapsait village in the Lelan division of [West Pokot District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Pokot_District "West Pokot District"). It is situated in the [Great Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley,_Kenya "Great Rift Valley, Kenya"), approximately 600 kilometres north of [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"). Her father and mother are from the [Pokot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokot_people "Pokot people") tribe, a [Nilotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_peoples "Nilotic peoples") ethnic group inhabiting parts of northern [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), eastern [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") and southern [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3)
Loroupe was told by her father that she was useless and her career might be babysitting.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3) She grew up with 24 siblings. The Pokots being a [polygamous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygamy "Polygamy") culture, her father had four wives. She spent her childhood working fields, tending cattle and looking after younger brothers and sisters.
At the age of six, Loroupe started school at Kapsait Elementary school; she had to run ten kilometers to and from school every morning. At school, she became aware of her potential as an [athlete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sportsperson "Sportsperson") when she won races held over a distance of 800 or 1500 meters against much older students. She decided to pursue a career as a runner. However, she was not supported by anyone but her mother.

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Loroupe%2C_Tegla.JPG/250px-Loroupe%2C_Tegla.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Loroupe,_Tegla.JPG)
Loroupe in 2007 at a meet in [Schortens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schortens "Schortens"), Germany.
The Kenyan athletics federation, [Athletics Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_Kenya "Athletics Kenya"), did not support her at first, thinking Loroupe too small and too thin. However, after she won a prestigious [cross country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-country_running "Cross-country running") barefoot race in 1988, this changed. She began to train to compete internationally the following year, earning her first pair of running shoes in 1989, which she wore only for particularly [rough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazard "Hazard") races. She was nominated for the junior race of the [1989 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1989 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") finishing 28th. She competed again at the [1990 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1990 IAAF World Cross Country Championships"), finishing 16th in the junior race.

In 1994 and 1998, Loroupe won the [Goodwill Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodwill_Games "Goodwill Games") over 10,000 metres, [barefoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barefoot_running "Barefoot running"). Over the same distance she won [bronze medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal "Bronze medal") at the [World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships") in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1995 World Championships in Athletics") and [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1999 World Championships in Athletics").
In 1994, Loroupe ran her first major [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_(sport) "Marathon (sport)") in New York. Running against the world's strongest competition, she won. As a consequence she was [idolised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolatry "Idolatry") by many young people in Africa: at last, a woman champion to complement the many successful male runners. She won the New York City Marathon again in 1995 and finished 3rd in 1998.
Between 1997 and 1999, she won three world titles a row over the half marathon distance. She won [Rotterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_Marathon "Rotterdam Marathon") three times between 1997 and 1999. She won [Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Marathon "Berlin Marathon") in 1999 and finished second in 2001. She finished second at the 1999 [Osaka International Ladies Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka_International_Ladies_Marathon "Osaka International Ladies Marathon").

Loroupe won the [Zevenheuvelenloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zevenheuvelenloop "Zevenheuvelenloop") 15K race in the Netherland three times (1992, 1993 and 1998). She is a seven-time [Egmond Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egmond_Half_Marathon "Egmond Half Marathon") winner (1993–1998, 2000). She has won the [Lisbon Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Half_Marathon "Lisbon Half Marathon") a record six times: 1994–1997, 1999 and 2000.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-4) She has won the [Tilburg road race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tilburg_Ten_Miles "Tilburg Ten Miles"), a five times (1993, 1994, 1996, 1998, 1999), also a record number. She won the [Paris Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Half_Marathon "Paris Half Marathon") in 1994 and 1998,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-5)[City-Pier-City Loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City-Pier-City_Loop "City-Pier-City Loop") half marathon in [the Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague") in 1998,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-6) and the [Parelloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parelloop "Parelloop") 10K in race in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") in 1999.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-7)

During the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") in Sydney, favoured to win both the marathon and the 10,000 meters, she suffered from violent food poisoning the night before the race. Nevertheless, she fought through the marathon race, finishing 13th, then, the next day, ran the 10,000 metres, finishing 5th,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-sr-1) running barefoot in both races, a feat she later stated she achieved out of a sense of duty to all the people taking her as a bearer of hope in her home country. Until the end of 2001, she continued to suffer from various health problems.
In 2000, she won [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") and [Rome City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome_City_Marathon "Rome City Marathon"). She also won [Lausanne Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lausanne_Marathon "Lausanne Marathon") in 2002, [Cologne Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne_Marathon "Cologne Marathon") in 2003 and [Leipzig Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leipzig_Marathon "Leipzig Marathon") in 2004.
Loroupe competed at the [2005 World Championships marathon race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics_-_Women's_Marathon "2005 World Championships in Athletics - Women's Marathon") in Helsinki, [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland"), but finished only 40th. In February 2006 she won the Hong Kong Half-Marathon. The same year she finished 5th in the Rotterdam Marathon and 2nd in the [Venice Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Marathon "Venice Marathon"). In 2007, she participated again the New York City Marathon, finishing 8th.

Loroupe's biggest successes include world records over 20, 25 and 30 kilometers as well as the past record over the marathon distance. She used to hold the [One Hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hour_run "Hour run") running [World record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_records_in_athletics "World records in athletics") of 18,340 m set in [Borgholzhausen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borgholzhausen "Borgholzhausen"), Germany, but the record was broken by Dire Tune of Ethiopia ten years later, in 2008 (new record 18,517 m).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-8)
In 2006, she was named a United Nations Ambassador of Sport by Secretary General [Kofi Annan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan "Kofi Annan"), together with [Roger Federer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Federer "Roger Federer"), tennis champion from Switzerland, [Elias Figueroa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elias_Figueroa "Elias Figueroa"), Latin American soccer legend from Chile, and [Katrina Webb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katrina_Webb "Katrina Webb") paralympics gold medalist from Australia. She is an International Sports Ambassador for the IAAF, the [International Association of Athletics Federations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Association_of_Athletics_Federations "International Association of Athletics Federations"), and for [UNICEF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF").
In 2003, Loroupe created an annual series of Peace Marathons sponsored by the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation "Peace Through Sports". Presidents, Prime Ministers, Ambassadors and government officials run with warriors and nomadic groups in her native Kenya, in Uganda and in Sudan, to bring peace to an area plagued by raiding warriors from battling tribes. In 2010 the Kenyan Government lauded her achievements as hundreds of warriors had laid down their weapons.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-9)

She has established a school ([Tegla Loroupe Peace Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe_Peace_Academy "Tegla Loroupe Peace Academy")) and orphanage for children from the region in [Kapenguria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapenguria "Kapenguria"), a high-mountain town in north-west [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya").
The 2006 Peace Marathon was held on 18 November 2006, in [Kapenguria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapenguria "Kapenguria"), Kenya. Two thousand warriors from six tribes competed. The next Peace Marathon was 15 November 2008 in Kapenguria, Kenya. National ambassadors to Kenya participated, together with the Prime Minister, and several Kenyan, Tanzanian, and Ugandan Ministers. The Peace Marathon has been held each year since then, with the exception of the past two Covid years. Winners of the races often begin professional training in long-distance running, or join the training team of ex-warriors.
In February 2007, she was named the [Oxfam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxfam "Oxfam") Ambassador of Sport and Peace to Darfur. In December 2006, she travelled with [George Clooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clooney "George Clooney"), [Joey Cheek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_Cheek "Joey Cheek"), and [Don Cheadle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Cheadle "Don Cheadle") to Beijing, Cairo, and New York on a diplomatic mission to bring an end to violence in Darfur. She won the "Community Hero" category at the 2007 [Kenyan Sports Personality of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_Sports_Personality_of_the_Year "Kenyan Sports Personality of the Year") awards.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-10)

In November 2009, Tegla represented the [Shoe4Africa team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoe4Africa_team?action=edit&redlink=1 "Shoe4Africa team (page does not exist)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-11) running the New York Marathon alongside founder Toby Tanser and actress [Sarah Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Jones_(stage_actress) "Sarah Jones (stage actress)")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-12) finishing in 3:54:02.
Loroupe is a member of the 'Champions for Peace' club, a group of 54 famous elite athletes committed to serving peace in the world through sport, created by [Peace and Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_and_Sport "Peace and Sport"), a [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco")-based international organisation.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-13)
As reported by Olympic news outlet [Around the Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Around_the_Rings "Around the Rings"), the IOC recognised six women, five from each continent and one to represent the world, for their achievements and their work to promote women's sport. Loroupe was awarded the world trophy.
In 2015 Loroupe became an Ambassador for the [Homeless World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeless_World_Cup "Homeless World Cup").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-14)

In 2016, she was the Chef de Mission organizing the [Refugee Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refugee_Olympic_Team_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Refugee Olympic Team at the 2016 Summer Olympics") for the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3) At those games Loroupe was inducted into the [Olympians for life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Olympians_Association#Olympians_for_Life "World Olympians Association") project for her work in promoting peace.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-15) In October 2016 Loroupe was awarded United Nations Person of the Year.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-16)

**Lornah Kiplagat** (born 1 May 1974) is a Dutch professional [long-distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_track_event "Long-distance track event")[runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running "Running"). She was born in [Kabiemit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keiyo_District "Keiyo District"), [Rift Valley Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift_Valley_Province "Rift Valley Province"), [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-1) and moved to the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") in 1999. She gained Dutch citizenship in 2003 and has competed for the Netherlands ever since.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-Lornah_@_Lornah.com-2) She used to run not only road events but also in [cross country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_country_running "Cross country running") and track and field.

She ran at the [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics"), [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") and [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics"), was the 2007 [gold medallist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_medal "Gold medal") at the [IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "IAAF World Cross Country Championships"), and took three straight World Road Running Championship titles from 2006 to 2008. In the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon"), she holds a best time of 2:22:22 hours and has won major races in [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_Marathon "Rotterdam Marathon"), [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Marathon "Amsterdam Marathon") and [Osaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka_Ladies_Marathon "Osaka Ladies Marathon"). She currently holds the [world road record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_athletics "List of world records in athletics") over 5 kilometres and 10 miles. Her best times over 20 km and the [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") distance were world records from 2007 to 2011 and remain the second fastest times ever.

Part of a highly successful family of runners, her relatives include [Sylvia Kibet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvia_Kibet "Sylvia Kibet"), [Hilda Kibet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilda_Kibet "Hilda Kibet") and [Susan Sirma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Sirma "Susan Sirma").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-4)
She is the founder of the famous high altitude training centre in [Iten, Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iten "Iten"). The centre is at 2400 metres high above sea level. Elite athletes and recreational runners from all over the world visit HATC every year for training. She is also the founder of her own African inspired sports brand called _Lornah_.
Kiplagat was already performing well when she ran for Kenya. She was the first woman to win both the [Falmouth Road Race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falmouth_Road_Race "Falmouth Road Race") and the [Peachtree Road Race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peachtree_Road_Race "Peachtree Road Race"). As of 2006 she is still the only woman to achieve this, but she achieved it three times in a row (2000, 2001 and 2002) and a fourth time in 2005 as well.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-5) Among her other achievements are the [Amsterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Marathon "Amsterdam Marathon"), the [Rotterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_Marathon "Rotterdam Marathon"), the [Osaka Ladies Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka_Ladies_Marathon "Osaka Ladies Marathon") and the [Los Angeles Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Marathon "Los Angeles Marathon").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-Lornah_@_Lornah.com-2)

In 1999 Kiplagat moved to the Netherlands; four years later she gained Dutch citizenship which allowed her to run for the Netherlands as of 2003. That same year she lowered the Dutch marathon record to 2:23.43 during the [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon"). She also participated in the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics"), where she finished 5th in the [10,000m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres").
The year 2005 was a successful one for Kiplagat: she won a silver medal at the [2005 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "2005 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships") then took the title at the [2005 European Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_European_Cross_Country_Championships "2005 European Cross Country Championships"), feats which led to her begin selected as the Dutch athlete of the year. At the [2006 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2006 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") she finished second in Japan, winning the silver medal. She also finished fifth in the 10,000m at the [2006 European Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_European_Athletics_Championships "2006 European Athletics Championships").

She won the [2007 World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2007 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") held in [Mombasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa "Mombasa"), Kenya. Earlier, in February 2007, she competed at the Kenyan Cross Country Championships as an invited athlete and won the women's race, ahead of the elite among her former compatriots.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-6) In winning these championships, she beat off the entire Ethiopian challenge, of defending champion [Tirunesh Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirunesh_Dibaba "Tirunesh Dibaba"), the previous short course champion [Gelete Burka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gelete_Burka "Gelete Burka"), and double bronze medalist from 2006, [Meselech Melkamu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meselech_Melkamu "Meselech Melkamu"). They finished: Dibaba, 2nd, Melkamu, 3rd, Burka, 4th.

Besides having owned the [Dutch record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_records_in_athletics "Dutch records in athletics") for the marathon from 2003 until 2022, Kiplagat also owns four [world records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_athletics "List of world records in athletics"). In the 5 km road race she ran the distance in 14:47, while she lowered her own record in the 10 miles of 50.54 by two seconds to 50.50 during the 2006 [Dam tot Damloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dam_tot_Damloop "Dam tot Damloop"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-7) which she also won in 2002. On 14 October 2007, Kiplagat set a new half marathon world record of 1:06:25 at the [World Road Running Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Road_Running_Championships "World Road Running Championships") at [Udine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udine "Udine"), Italy, while defending the title she first won in 2006. She also smashed her own 20 km world record en route, running 1:02:57. However, [Paula Radcliffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe "Paula Radcliffe") has run a faster half-marathon on the slightly downhill [Great North Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Run "Great North Run") course in 2003.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-8)

Kiplagat was ruled out for the whole of 2009 and returned to competition with a win at the [Runner's World Zandvoort Circuit Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runner's_World_Zandvoort_Circuit_Run?action=edit&redlink=1 "Runner's World Zandvoort Circuit Run (page does not exist)") in March 2010.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-9) In September, she ran at the Dam tot Damloop and was the runner-up behind her niece Hilda Kibet, finishing with a time of 52:03.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-10) She returned to the marathon event for the [2011 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_London_Marathon "2011 London Marathon") and completed her first race over the distance in four years, coming 18th with a time of 2:27:57 hours. Although she was far from the podium and failed to gain the World Championship qualifying time, she considered the race a success following her previous injury-ridden seasons.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-11) She improved at the 2011 Amsterdam Marathon, crossing the line after 2:25:52 hours to claim third place, the Dutch national title, and the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") qualifying time. Despite being almost four minutes slower than the winner ([Tiki Gelana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiki_Gelana "Tiki Gelana")), she said: "I am the happiest woman in Amsterdam, and perhaps the whole world".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-12)

Tegla Loroupe (9 May 1973 – ) is a former Kenyan long-distance track and road runner. She was the first African woman to win the New York City Marathon. She won twice, once with the highest temperature recorded for the New York Marathon, once with the lowest temperature recorded. She has held many world records.
Tegla Loroupe was born in Kutomwony in the West Pokot District of Keyna – situated in the Rift Valley, north of Nairobi. Tegla grew up with 24 siblings; her father had four wives. She spent her childhood working in the fields and looking after younger brothers and sisters. From an early age, Loroupe was given a nickname – Chametia. It means “the one who never gets annoyed.” – reflecting her cheerful personality.

#### Sports Achievements
In 1994, Loroupe ran her first major marathon in New York and won. She was the first African woman to win the New York Marathon. As a consequence, she became an important sporting role model. Kenya, at last, had a female runner to rank alongside its talented male athletes.
After this initial success, Tegla Loroupe went on to win many major marathons around the world. Between 1997 and 1999, she won three consecutive world half marathon Championships. In the World Championships, she won bronze in the 10,000m in both 1995 and 1999. Between 19 April 1998 – 30 September 2001, Loroupe held the world record for the marathon. She initially set a time of 2:20:47 in the 1998 Rotterdam marathon. In 1999, she broke her own record, setting a time of 2:20:43 in the Berlin marathon. She has also held world records at one hour, 20, 25 and 30 kilometres.
The marathon proved to be Loroupe’s most successful distance. She won the marathons of Rotterdam three times between 1997 and 1999, New York in 1994 and 1995, Berlin in 1999, London and Rome in 2000 and Lausanne in 2002. Loroupe holds the world records for 20, 25 and 30 kilometres and previously held the world marathon record. She is the three-time World Half-Marathon champion. She has won marathons in London, Boston, Rotterdam, Hong Kong, Berlin, Rome and many other cities.
In 2003, Loroupe founded the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation and has been an active advocate for peace. She has been successful in bringing members of warring tribes together in conflict areas in East Africa.

#### Sports Achievements
In 2006, she founded the 10km Peace Race, which included 2,000 warriors from six different tribes, who put down their weapon to run in peace in Kapenguria, Kenya. Loroupe said the motivation for the race was to use her fame to help bring about greater harmony.
In 2006, the Secretary of the United Nations, Kofe Annan, named her the United Nations Peace Ambassador, together with Roger Federer, in the United Nations Year of Sport.
She is also a member of the ‘Champions for Peace’ a group of athletes seeking to use the power of sport to bring about peace. Loroupe has also sought to advance the opportunities of Kenyan women. She is a role model and has helped many women widen their horizons and enter new fields in peace-making, education, and sports.
Tegla Loroupe was born in Kapsait village in the Lelan division of[West Pokot District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Pokot_District "West Pokot District"). It is situated in the[Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley,_Kenya "Great Rift Valley, Kenya"), approximately 600 kilometres north of[Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"). **Tegla Chepkite Loroupe** (born 9 May 1973) is a former Kenyan [long-distance track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_track_event "Long-distance track event") and [road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") runner. She is also a global spokeswoman for peace, [women's rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_rights "Women's rights") and education. Loroupe holds the [world records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_record "World record") for 25 and 30 kilometers and previously held the world [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") record. She was the first African woman to hold the marathon World Record, which she held from 19 April 1998 until 30 September 2001. She is the three-time [World Half-Marathon champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "IAAF World Half Marathon Championships"). Loroupe was also the first woman from Africa to win the [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon"), which she has won twice. She has won marathons in London, [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam"), Hong Kong, [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin") and Rome.
In 2016, she was the person organizing the Refugee Team for the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics") in Rio.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3)
texts.8:
Tegla Loroupe was born in Kapsait village in the Lelan division of [West Pokot District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Pokot_District "West Pokot District"). It is situated in the [Great Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley,_Kenya "Great Rift Valley, Kenya"), approximately 600 kilometres north of [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"). Her father and mother are from the [Pokot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokot_people "Pokot people") tribe, a [Nilotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_peoples "Nilotic peoples") ethnic group inhabiting parts of northern [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), eastern [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") and southern [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3)
Loroupe was told by her father that she was useless and her career might be babysitting.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3) She grew up with 24 siblings. The Pokots being a [polygamous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygamy "Polygamy") culture, her father had four wives. She spent her childhood working fields, tending cattle and looking after younger brothers and sisters.
At the age of six, Loroupe started school at Kapsait Elementary school; she had to run ten kilometers to and from school every morning. At school, she became aware of her potential as an [athlete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sportsperson "Sportsperson") when she won races held over a distance of 800 or 1500 meters against much older students. She decided to pursue a career as a runner. However, she was not supported by anyone but her mother.
texts.9:
[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Loroupe%2C_Tegla.JPG/250px-Loroupe%2C_Tegla.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Loroupe,_Tegla.JPG)
Loroupe in 2007 at a meet in [Schortens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schortens "Schortens"), Germany.
The Kenyan athletics federation, [Athletics Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_Kenya "Athletics Kenya"), did not support her at first, thinking Loroupe too small and too thin. However, after she won a prestigious [cross country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-country_running "Cross-country running") barefoot race in 1988, this changed. She began to train to compete internationally the following year, earning her first pair of running shoes in 1989, which she wore only for particularly [rough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazard "Hazard") races. She was nominated for the junior race of the [1989 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1989 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") finishing 28th. She competed again at the [1990 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1990 IAAF World Cross Country Championships"), finishing 16th in the junior race.
texts.10:
In 1994 and 1998, Loroupe won the [Goodwill Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodwill_Games "Goodwill Games") over 10,000 metres, [barefoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barefoot_running "Barefoot running"). Over the same distance she won [bronze medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal "Bronze medal") at the [World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships") in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1995 World Championships in Athletics") and [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1999 World Championships in Athletics").
In 1994, Loroupe ran her first major [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_(sport) "Marathon (sport)") in New York. Running against the world's strongest competition, she won. As a consequence she was [idolised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolatry "Idolatry") by many young people in Africa: at last, a woman champion to complement the many successful male runners. She won the New York City Marathon again in 1995 and finished 3rd in 1998.
Between 1997 and 1999, she won three world titles a row over the half marathon distance. She won [Rotterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_Marathon "Rotterdam Marathon") three times between 1997 and 1999. She won [Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Marathon "Berlin Marathon") in 1999 and finished second in 2001. She finished second at the 1999 [Osaka International Ladies Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka_International_Ladies_Marathon "Osaka International Ladies Marathon").
texts.11: Loroupe won the [Zevenheuvelenloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zevenheuvelenloop "Zevenheuvelenloop") 15K race in the Netherland three times (1992, 1993 and 1998). She is a seven-time [Egmond Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egmond_Half_Marathon "Egmond Half Marathon") winner (1993–1998, 2000). She has won the [Lisbon Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Half_Marathon "Lisbon Half Marathon") a record six times: 1994–1997, 1999 and 2000.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-4) She has won the [Tilburg road race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tilburg_Ten_Miles "Tilburg Ten Miles"), a five times (1993, 1994, 1996, 1998, 1999), also a record number. She won the [Paris Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Half_Marathon "Paris Half Marathon") in 1994 and 1998,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-5)[City-Pier-City Loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City-Pier-City_Loop "City-Pier-City Loop") half marathon in [the Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague") in 1998,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-6) and the [Parelloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parelloop "Parelloop") 10K in race in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") in 1999.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-7)
texts.12:
During the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") in Sydney, favoured to win both the marathon and the 10,000 meters, she suffered from violent food poisoning the night before the race. Nevertheless, she fought through the marathon race, finishing 13th, then, the next day, ran the 10,000 metres, finishing 5th,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-sr-1) running barefoot in both races, a feat she later stated she achieved out of a sense of duty to all the people taking her as a bearer of hope in her home country. Until the end of 2001, she continued to suffer from various health problems.
In 2000, she won [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") and [Rome City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome_City_Marathon "Rome City Marathon"). She also won [Lausanne Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lausanne_Marathon "Lausanne Marathon") in 2002, [Cologne Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne_Marathon "Cologne Marathon") in 2003 and [Leipzig Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leipzig_Marathon "Leipzig Marathon") in 2004.
Loroupe competed at the [2005 World Championships marathon race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics_-_Women's_Marathon "2005 World Championships in Athletics - Women's Marathon") in Helsinki, [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland"), but finished only 40th. In February 2006 she won the Hong Kong Half-Marathon. The same year she finished 5th in the Rotterdam Marathon and 2nd in the [Venice Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Marathon "Venice Marathon"). In 2007, she participated again the New York City Marathon, finishing 8th.
texts.13:
Loroupe's biggest successes include world records over 20, 25 and 30 kilometers as well as the past record over the marathon distance. She used to hold the [One Hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hour_run "Hour run") running [World record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_records_in_athletics "World records in athletics") of 18,340 m set in [Borgholzhausen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borgholzhausen "Borgholzhausen"), Germany, but the record was broken by Dire Tune of Ethiopia ten years later, in 2008 (new record 18,517 m).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-8)
In 2006, she was named a United Nations Ambassador of Sport by Secretary General [Kofi Annan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan "Kofi Annan"), together with [Roger Federer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Federer "Roger Federer"), tennis champion from Switzerland, [Elias Figueroa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elias_Figueroa "Elias Figueroa"), Latin American soccer legend from Chile, and [Katrina Webb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katrina_Webb "Katrina Webb") paralympics gold medalist from Australia. She is an International Sports Ambassador for the IAAF, the [International Association of Athletics Federations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Association_of_Athletics_Federations "International Association of Athletics Federations"), and for [UNICEF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF").
In 2003, Loroupe created an annual series of Peace Marathons sponsored by the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation "Peace Through Sports". Presidents, Prime Ministers, Ambassadors and government officials run with warriors and nomadic groups in her native Kenya, in Uganda and in Sudan, to bring peace to an area plagued by raiding warriors from battling tribes. In 2010 the Kenyan Government lauded her achievements as hundreds of warriors had laid down their weapons.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-9)
texts.14:
She has established a school ([Tegla Loroupe Peace Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe_Peace_Academy "Tegla Loroupe Peace Academy")) and orphanage for children from the region in [Kapenguria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapenguria "Kapenguria"), a high-mountain town in north-west [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya").
The 2006 Peace Marathon was held on 18 November 2006, in [Kapenguria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapenguria "Kapenguria"), Kenya. Two thousand warriors from six tribes competed. The next Peace Marathon was 15 November 2008 in Kapenguria, Kenya. National ambassadors to Kenya participated, together with the Prime Minister, and several Kenyan, Tanzanian, and Ugandan Ministers. The Peace Marathon has been held each year since then, with the exception of the past two Covid years. Winners of the races often begin professional training in long-distance running, or join the training team of ex-warriors.
In February 2007, she was named the [Oxfam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxfam "Oxfam") Ambassador of Sport and Peace to Darfur. In December 2006, she travelled with [George Clooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clooney "George Clooney"), [Joey Cheek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_Cheek "Joey Cheek"), and [Don Cheadle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Cheadle "Don Cheadle") to Beijing, Cairo, and New York on a diplomatic mission to bring an end to violence in Darfur. She won the "Community Hero" category at the 2007 [Kenyan Sports Personality of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_Sports_Personality_of_the_Year "Kenyan Sports Personality of the Year") awards.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-10)
texts.15:
In November 2009, Tegla represented the [Shoe4Africa team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoe4Africa_team?action=edit&redlink=1 "Shoe4Africa team (page does not exist)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-11) running the New York Marathon alongside founder Toby Tanser and actress [Sarah Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Jones_(stage_actress) "Sarah Jones (stage actress)")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-12) finishing in 3:54:02.
Loroupe is a member of the 'Champions for Peace' club, a group of 54 famous elite athletes committed to serving peace in the world through sport, created by [Peace and Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_and_Sport "Peace and Sport"), a [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco")-based international organisation.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-13)
As reported by Olympic news outlet [Around the Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Around_the_Rings "Around the Rings"), the IOC recognised six women, five from each continent and one to represent the world, for their achievements and their work to promote women's sport. Loroupe was awarded the world trophy.
In 2015 Loroupe became an Ambassador for the [Homeless World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeless_World_Cup "Homeless World Cup").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-14)
texts.16: In 2016, she was the Chef de Mission organizing the [Refugee Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refugee_Olympic_Team_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Refugee Olympic Team at the 2016 Summer Olympics") for the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3) At those games Loroupe was inducted into the [Olympians for life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Olympians_Association#Olympians_for_Life "World Olympians Association") project for her work in promoting peace.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-15) In October 2016 Loroupe was awarded United Nations Person of the Year.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-16)

Tegla Loroupe (9 May 1973 – ) is a former Kenyan long-distance track and road runner. She was the first African woman to win the New York City Marathon. She won twice, once with the highest temperature recorded for the New York Marathon, once with the lowest temperature recorded. She has held many world records.
Tegla Loroupe was born in Kutomwony in the West Pokot District of Keyna – situated in the Rift Valley, north of Nairobi. Tegla grew up with 24 siblings; her father had four wives. She spent her childhood working in the fields and looking after younger brothers and sisters. From an early age, Loroupe was given a nickname – Chametia. It means “the one who never gets annoyed.” – reflecting her cheerful personality.
texts.1:
#### Sports Achievements
In 1994, Loroupe ran her first major marathon in New York and won. She was the first African woman to win the New York Marathon. As a consequence, she became an important sporting role model. Kenya, at last, had a female runner to rank alongside its talented male athletes.
After this initial success, Tegla Loroupe went on to win many major marathons around the world. Between 1997 and 1999, she won three consecutive world half marathon Championships. In the World Championships, she won bronze in the 10,000m in both 1995 and 1999. Between 19 April 1998 – 30 September 2001, Loroupe held the world record for the marathon. She initially set a time of 2:20:47 in the 1998 Rotterdam marathon. In 1999, she broke her own record, setting a time of 2:20:43 in the Berlin marathon. She has also held world records at one hour, 20, 25 and 30 kilometres.
The marathon proved to be Loroupe’s most successful distance. She won the marathons of Rotterdam three times between 1997 and 1999, New York in 1994 and 1995, Berlin in 1999, London and Rome in 2000 and Lausanne in 2002. Loroupe holds the world records for 20, 25 and 30 kilometres and previously held the world marathon record. She is the three-time World Half-Marathon champion. She has won marathons in London, Boston, Rotterdam, Hong Kong, Berlin, Rome and many other cities.
In 2003, Loroupe founded the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation and has been an active advocate for peace. She has been successful in bringing members of warring tribes together in conflict areas in East Africa.
texts.2:
#### Sports Achievements
In 2006, she founded the 10km Peace Race, which included 2,000 warriors from six different tribes, who put down their weapon to run in peace in Kapenguria, Kenya. Loroupe said the motivation for the race was to use her fame to help bring about greater harmony.
In 2006, the Secretary of the United Nations, Kofe Annan, named her the United Nations Peace Ambassador, together with Roger Federer, in the United Nations Year of Sport.
She is also a member of the ‘Champions for Peace’ a group of athletes seeking to use the power of sport to bring about peace. Loroupe has also sought to advance the opportunities of Kenyan women. She is a role model and has helped many women widen their horizons and enter new fields in peace-making, education, and sports.
Tegla Loroupe was born in Kapsait village in the Lelan division of[West Pokot District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Pokot_District "West Pokot District"). It is situated in the[Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley,_Kenya "Great Rift Valley, Kenya"), approximately 600 kilometres north of[Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"). Her father and mother are from the[Pokot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokot_people "Pokot people")tribe, a[Nilotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_peoples "Nilotic peoples")ethnic group inhabiting parts of northern[Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), eastern[Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda")and southern[Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia").[[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3)

texts.4: **Lornah Kiplagat** (born 1 May 1974) is a Dutch professional [long-distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_track_event "Long-distance track event")[runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running "Running"). She was born in [Kabiemit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keiyo_District "Keiyo District"), [Rift Valley Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift_Valley_Province "Rift Valley Province"), [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-1) and moved to the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") in 1999. She gained Dutch citizenship in 2003 and has competed for the Netherlands ever since.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-Lornah_@_Lornah.com-2) She used to run not only road events but also in [cross country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_country_running "Cross country running") and track and field.
texts.5: She ran at the [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics"), [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") and [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics"), was the 2007 [gold medallist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_medal "Gold medal") at the [IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "IAAF World Cross Country Championships"), and took three straight World Road Running Championship titles from 2006 to 2008. In the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon"), she holds a best time of 2:22:22 hours and has won major races in [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_Marathon "Rotterdam Marathon"), [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Marathon "Amsterdam Marathon") and [Osaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka_Ladies_Marathon "Osaka Ladies Marathon"). She currently holds the [world road record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_athletics "List of world records in athletics") over 5 kilometres and 10 miles. Her best times over 20 km and the [half marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half_marathon "Half marathon") distance were world records from 2007 to 2011 and remain the second fastest times ever.
texts.6:
Part of a highly successful family of runners, her relatives include [Sylvia Kibet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvia_Kibet "Sylvia Kibet"), [Hilda Kibet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilda_Kibet "Hilda Kibet") and [Susan Sirma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Sirma "Susan Sirma").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-4)
She is the founder of the famous high altitude training centre in [Iten, Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iten "Iten"). The centre is at 2400 metres high above sea level. Elite athletes and recreational runners from all over the world visit HATC every year for training. She is also the founder of her own African inspired sports brand called _Lornah_.
Kiplagat was already performing well when she ran for Kenya. She was the first woman to win both the [Falmouth Road Race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falmouth_Road_Race "Falmouth Road Race") and the [Peachtree Road Race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peachtree_Road_Race "Peachtree Road Race"). As of 2006 she is still the only woman to achieve this, but she achieved it three times in a row (2000, 2001 and 2002) and a fourth time in 2005 as well.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-5) Among her other achievements are the [Amsterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Marathon "Amsterdam Marathon"), the [Rotterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_Marathon "Rotterdam Marathon"), the [Osaka Ladies Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka_Ladies_Marathon "Osaka Ladies Marathon") and the [Los Angeles Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Marathon "Los Angeles Marathon").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-Lornah_@_Lornah.com-2)
texts.7:
In 1999 Kiplagat moved to the Netherlands; four years later she gained Dutch citizenship which allowed her to run for the Netherlands as of 2003. That same year she lowered the Dutch marathon record to 2:23.43 during the [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon"). She also participated in the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics"), where she finished 5th in the [10,000m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres").
The year 2005 was a successful one for Kiplagat: she won a silver medal at the [2005 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "2005 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships") then took the title at the [2005 European Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_European_Cross_Country_Championships "2005 European Cross Country Championships"), feats which led to her begin selected as the Dutch athlete of the year. At the [2006 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2006 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") she finished second in Japan, winning the silver medal. She also finished fifth in the 10,000m at the [2006 European Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_European_Athletics_Championships "2006 European Athletics Championships").
texts.8: She won the [2007 World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2007 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") held in [Mombasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mombasa "Mombasa"), Kenya. Earlier, in February 2007, she competed at the Kenyan Cross Country Championships as an invited athlete and won the women's race, ahead of the elite among her former compatriots.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-6) In winning these championships, she beat off the entire Ethiopian challenge, of defending champion [Tirunesh Dibaba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirunesh_Dibaba "Tirunesh Dibaba"), the previous short course champion [Gelete Burka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gelete_Burka "Gelete Burka"), and double bronze medalist from 2006, [Meselech Melkamu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meselech_Melkamu "Meselech Melkamu"). They finished: Dibaba, 2nd, Melkamu, 3rd, Burka, 4th.
texts.9: Besides having owned the [Dutch record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_records_in_athletics "Dutch records in athletics") for the marathon from 2003 until 2022, Kiplagat also owns four [world records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_athletics "List of world records in athletics"). In the 5 km road race she ran the distance in 14:47, while she lowered her own record in the 10 miles of 50.54 by two seconds to 50.50 during the 2006 [Dam tot Damloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dam_tot_Damloop "Dam tot Damloop"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-7) which she also won in 2002. On 14 October 2007, Kiplagat set a new half marathon world record of 1:06:25 at the [World Road Running Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Road_Running_Championships "World Road Running Championships") at [Udine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udine "Udine"), Italy, while defending the title she first won in 2006. She also smashed her own 20 km world record en route, running 1:02:57. However, [Paula Radcliffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe "Paula Radcliffe") has run a faster half-marathon on the slightly downhill [Great North Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Run "Great North Run") course in 2003.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-8)
texts.10: Kiplagat was ruled out for the whole of 2009 and returned to competition with a win at the [Runner's World Zandvoort Circuit Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runner's_World_Zandvoort_Circuit_Run?action=edit&redlink=1 "Runner's World Zandvoort Circuit Run (page does not exist)") in March 2010.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-9) In September, she ran at the Dam tot Damloop and was the runner-up behind her niece Hilda Kibet, finishing with a time of 52:03.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-10) She returned to the marathon event for the [2011 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_London_Marathon "2011 London Marathon") and completed her first race over the distance in four years, coming 18th with a time of 2:27:57 hours. Although she was far from the podium and failed to gain the World Championship qualifying time, she considered the race a success following her previous injury-ridden seasons.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-11) She improved at the 2011 Amsterdam Marathon, crossing the line after 2:25:52 hours to claim third place, the Dutch national title, and the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") qualifying time. Despite being almost four minutes slower than the winner ([Tiki Gelana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiki_Gelana "Tiki Gelana")), she said: "I am the happiest woman in Amsterdam, and perhaps the whole world".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lornah_Kiplagat#cite_note-12)

**Tegla Chepkite Loroupe** (born 9 May 1973) is a former Kenyan [long-distance track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_track_event "Long-distance track event") and [road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") runner. She is also a global spokeswoman for peace, [women's rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_rights "Women's rights") and education. Loroupe holds the [world records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_record "World record") for 25 and 30 kilometers and previously held the world [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") record. She was the first African woman to hold the marathon World Record, which she held from 19 April 1998 until 30 September 2001. She is the three-time [World Half-Marathon champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "IAAF World Half Marathon Championships"). Loroupe was also the first woman from Africa to win the [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon"), which she has won twice. She has won marathons in London, [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam"), Hong Kong, [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin") and Rome.
In 2016, she was the person organizing the Refugee Team for the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics") in Rio.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3)

Tegla Loroupe was born in Kapsait village in the Lelan division of [West Pokot District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Pokot_District "West Pokot District"). It is situated in the [Great Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley,_Kenya "Great Rift Valley, Kenya"), approximately 600 kilometres north of [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"). Her father and mother are from the [Pokot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokot_people "Pokot people") tribe, a [Nilotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_peoples "Nilotic peoples") ethnic group inhabiting parts of northern [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), eastern [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") and southern [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3)
Loroupe was told by her father that she was useless and her career might be babysitting.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3) She grew up with 24 siblings. The Pokots being a [polygamous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygamy "Polygamy") culture, her father had four wives. She spent her childhood working fields, tending cattle and looking after younger brothers and sisters.
At the age of six, Loroupe started school at Kapsait Elementary school; she had to run ten kilometers to and from school every morning. At school, she became aware of her potential as an [athlete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sportsperson "Sportsperson") when she won races held over a distance of 800 or 1500 meters against much older students. She decided to pursue a career as a runner. However, she was not supported by anyone but her mother.

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Loroupe%2C_Tegla.JPG/250px-Loroupe%2C_Tegla.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Loroupe,_Tegla.JPG)
Loroupe in 2007 at a meet in [Schortens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schortens "Schortens"), Germany.
The Kenyan athletics federation, [Athletics Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_Kenya "Athletics Kenya"), did not support her at first, thinking Loroupe too small and too thin. However, after she won a prestigious [cross country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-country_running "Cross-country running") barefoot race in 1988, this changed. She began to train to compete internationally the following year, earning her first pair of running shoes in 1989, which she wore only for particularly [rough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazard "Hazard") races. She was nominated for the junior race of the [1989 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1989 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") finishing 28th. She competed again at the [1990 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1990 IAAF World Cross Country Championships"), finishing 16th in the junior race.

In 1994 and 1998, Loroupe won the [Goodwill Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodwill_Games "Goodwill Games") over 10,000 metres, [barefoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barefoot_running "Barefoot running"). Over the same distance she won [bronze medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal "Bronze medal") at the [World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships") in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1995 World Championships in Athletics") and [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1999 World Championships in Athletics").
In 1994, Loroupe ran her first major [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_(sport) "Marathon (sport)") in New York. Running against the world's strongest competition, she won. As a consequence she was [idolised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolatry "Idolatry") by many young people in Africa: at last, a woman champion to complement the many successful male runners. She won the New York City Marathon again in 1995 and finished 3rd in 1998.
Between 1997 and 1999, she won three world titles a row over the half marathon distance. She won [Rotterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_Marathon "Rotterdam Marathon") three times between 1997 and 1999. She won [Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Marathon "Berlin Marathon") in 1999 and finished second in 2001. She finished second at the 1999 [Osaka International Ladies Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka_International_Ladies_Marathon "Osaka International Ladies Marathon").

Loroupe won the [Zevenheuvelenloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zevenheuvelenloop "Zevenheuvelenloop") 15K race in the Netherland three times (1992, 1993 and 1998). She is a seven-time [Egmond Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egmond_Half_Marathon "Egmond Half Marathon") winner (1993–1998, 2000). She has won the [Lisbon Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Half_Marathon "Lisbon Half Marathon") a record six times: 1994–1997, 1999 and 2000.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-4) She has won the [Tilburg road race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tilburg_Ten_Miles "Tilburg Ten Miles"), a five times (1993, 1994, 1996, 1998, 1999), also a record number. She won the [Paris Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Half_Marathon "Paris Half Marathon") in 1994 and 1998,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-5)[City-Pier-City Loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City-Pier-City_Loop "City-Pier-City Loop") half marathon in [the Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague") in 1998,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-6) and the [Parelloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parelloop "Parelloop") 10K in race in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") in 1999.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-7)

During the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") in Sydney, favoured to win both the marathon and the 10,000 meters, she suffered from violent food poisoning the night before the race. Nevertheless, she fought through the marathon race, finishing 13th, then, the next day, ran the 10,000 metres, finishing 5th,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-sr-1) running barefoot in both races, a feat she later stated she achieved out of a sense of duty to all the people taking her as a bearer of hope in her home country. Until the end of 2001, she continued to suffer from various health problems.
In 2000, she won [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") and [Rome City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome_City_Marathon "Rome City Marathon"). She also won [Lausanne Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lausanne_Marathon "Lausanne Marathon") in 2002, [Cologne Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne_Marathon "Cologne Marathon") in 2003 and [Leipzig Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leipzig_Marathon "Leipzig Marathon") in 2004.
Loroupe competed at the [2005 World Championships marathon race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics_-_Women's_Marathon "2005 World Championships in Athletics - Women's Marathon") in Helsinki, [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland"), but finished only 40th. In February 2006 she won the Hong Kong Half-Marathon. The same year she finished 5th in the Rotterdam Marathon and 2nd in the [Venice Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Marathon "Venice Marathon"). In 2007, she participated again the New York City Marathon, finishing 8th.

Loroupe's biggest successes include world records over 20, 25 and 30 kilometers as well as the past record over the marathon distance. She used to hold the [One Hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hour_run "Hour run") running [World record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_records_in_athletics "World records in athletics") of 18,340 m set in [Borgholzhausen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borgholzhausen "Borgholzhausen"), Germany, but the record was broken by Dire Tune of Ethiopia ten years later, in 2008 (new record 18,517 m).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-8)
In 2006, she was named a United Nations Ambassador of Sport by Secretary General [Kofi Annan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan "Kofi Annan"), together with [Roger Federer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Federer "Roger Federer"), tennis champion from Switzerland, [Elias Figueroa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elias_Figueroa "Elias Figueroa"), Latin American soccer legend from Chile, and [Katrina Webb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katrina_Webb "Katrina Webb") paralympics gold medalist from Australia. She is an International Sports Ambassador for the IAAF, the [International Association of Athletics Federations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Association_of_Athletics_Federations "International Association of Athletics Federations"), and for [UNICEF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF").
In 2003, Loroupe created an annual series of Peace Marathons sponsored by the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation "Peace Through Sports". Presidents, Prime Ministers, Ambassadors and government officials run with warriors and nomadic groups in her native Kenya, in Uganda and in Sudan, to bring peace to an area plagued by raiding warriors from battling tribes. In 2010 the Kenyan Government lauded her achievements as hundreds of warriors had laid down their weapons.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-9)

She has established a school ([Tegla Loroupe Peace Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe_Peace_Academy "Tegla Loroupe Peace Academy")) and orphanage for children from the region in [Kapenguria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapenguria "Kapenguria"), a high-mountain town in north-west [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya").
The 2006 Peace Marathon was held on 18 November 2006, in [Kapenguria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapenguria "Kapenguria"), Kenya. Two thousand warriors from six tribes competed. The next Peace Marathon was 15 November 2008 in Kapenguria, Kenya. National ambassadors to Kenya participated, together with the Prime Minister, and several Kenyan, Tanzanian, and Ugandan Ministers. The Peace Marathon has been held each year since then, with the exception of the past two Covid years. Winners of the races often begin professional training in long-distance running, or join the training team of ex-warriors.
In February 2007, she was named the [Oxfam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxfam "Oxfam") Ambassador of Sport and Peace to Darfur. In December 2006, she travelled with [George Clooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clooney "George Clooney"), [Joey Cheek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_Cheek "Joey Cheek"), and [Don Cheadle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Cheadle "Don Cheadle") to Beijing, Cairo, and New York on a diplomatic mission to bring an end to violence in Darfur. She won the "Community Hero" category at the 2007 [Kenyan Sports Personality of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_Sports_Personality_of_the_Year "Kenyan Sports Personality of the Year") awards.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-10)

In November 2009, Tegla represented the [Shoe4Africa team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoe4Africa_team?action=edit&redlink=1 "Shoe4Africa team (page does not exist)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-11) running the New York Marathon alongside founder Toby Tanser and actress [Sarah Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Jones_(stage_actress) "Sarah Jones (stage actress)")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-12) finishing in 3:54:02.
Loroupe is a member of the 'Champions for Peace' club, a group of 54 famous elite athletes committed to serving peace in the world through sport, created by [Peace and Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_and_Sport "Peace and Sport"), a [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco")-based international organisation.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-13)
As reported by Olympic news outlet [Around the Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Around_the_Rings "Around the Rings"), the IOC recognised six women, five from each continent and one to represent the world, for their achievements and their work to promote women's sport. Loroupe was awarded the world trophy.
In 2015 Loroupe became an Ambassador for the [Homeless World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeless_World_Cup "Homeless World Cup").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-14)

In 2016, she was the Chef de Mission organizing the [Refugee Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refugee_Olympic_Team_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Refugee Olympic Team at the 2016 Summer Olympics") for the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3) At those games Loroupe was inducted into the [Olympians for life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Olympians_Association#Olympians_for_Life "World Olympians Association") project for her work in promoting peace.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-15) In October 2016 Loroupe was awarded United Nations Person of the Year.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-16)

Tegla Loroupe (9 May 1973 – ) is a former Kenyan long-distance track and road runner. She was the first African woman to win the New York City Marathon. She won twice, once with the highest temperature recorded for the New York Marathon, once with the lowest temperature recorded. She has held many world records.
Tegla Loroupe was born in Kutomwony in the West Pokot District of Keyna – situated in the Rift Valley, north of Nairobi. Tegla grew up with 24 siblings; her father had four wives. She spent her childhood working in the fields and looking after younger brothers and sisters. From an early age, Loroupe was given a nickname – Chametia. It means “the one who never gets annoyed.” – reflecting her cheerful personality.

#### Sports Achievements
In 1994, Loroupe ran her first major marathon in New York and won. She was the first African woman to win the New York Marathon. As a consequence, she became an important sporting role model. Kenya, at last, had a female runner to rank alongside its talented male athletes.
After this initial success, Tegla Loroupe went on to win many major marathons around the world. Between 1997 and 1999, she won three consecutive world half marathon Championships. In the World Championships, she won bronze in the 10,000m in both 1995 and 1999. Between 19 April 1998 – 30 September 2001, Loroupe held the world record for the marathon. She initially set a time of 2:20:47 in the 1998 Rotterdam marathon. In 1999, she broke her own record, setting a time of 2:20:43 in the Berlin marathon. She has also held world records at one hour, 20, 25 and 30 kilometres.
The marathon proved to be Loroupe’s most successful distance. She won the marathons of Rotterdam three times between 1997 and 1999, New York in 1994 and 1995, Berlin in 1999, London and Rome in 2000 and Lausanne in 2002. Loroupe holds the world records for 20, 25 and 30 kilometres and previously held the world marathon record. She is the three-time World Half-Marathon champion. She has won marathons in London, Boston, Rotterdam, Hong Kong, Berlin, Rome and many other cities.
In 2003, Loroupe founded the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation and has been an active advocate for peace. She has been successful in bringing members of warring tribes together in conflict areas in East Africa.

#### Sports Achievements
In 2006, she founded the 10km Peace Race, which included 2,000 warriors from six different tribes, who put down their weapon to run in peace in Kapenguria, Kenya. Loroupe said the motivation for the race was to use her fame to help bring about greater harmony.
In 2006, the Secretary of the United Nations, Kofe Annan, named her the United Nations Peace Ambassador, together with Roger Federer, in the United Nations Year of Sport.
She is also a member of the ‘Champions for Peace’ a group of athletes seeking to use the power of sport to bring about peace. Loroupe has also sought to advance the opportunities of Kenyan women. She is a role model and has helped many women widen their horizons and enter new fields in peace-making, education, and sports.
Tegla Loroupe was born in Kapsait village in the Lelan division of[West Pokot District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Pokot_District "West Pokot District"). It is situated in the[Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley,_Kenya "Great Rift Valley, Kenya"), approximately 600 kilometres north of[Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"). Her father and mother are from the[Pokot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokot_people "Pokot people")tribe, a[Nilotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_peoples "Nilotic peoples")ethnic group inhabiting parts of northern[Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), eastern[Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda")and southern[Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia").[[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3)
